newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth plans new unit to sell service - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth plans new unit to sell service - WSJ.

text.p: BellSouth Corp plans to set up a new unit for selling telecom and entertainment services in an attempt to escape some regulations that hinder it while pursuing customers outside its traditional Southeastern markets, the Wall Street Journal reported.

The paper said in its electronic edition on Tuesday that Richard Anderson, the company's vice president of marketing, plans to ask regulators for permission to operate the unit as a "competitive local" phone company throughout its nine-state territory.
The unit would be closely linked to its parent company, the paper added.
It would offer a range of telecommunications and entertainment services, including basic local-phone service, Internet connections, cellular fare and video offerings, the paper said.
Regulators would probably take a close look at the structure of the proposed unit, the paper said.
